query: What visit-note signals suggest a longer visit?

per_column.name: num_conditions
per_column.rationale: Clinical complexity is a strong plausible driver of visit length, giving a genuine grouping/modeling axis. However groundedness is shaky: the URI note counts '4' conditions and the knee-injury note '1' in ways not clearly supported by distinct diagnoses in the text; counts appear inflated/inconsistent.

per_column.name: has_procedure
per_column.rationale: Whether a procedure occurred is a meaningful and non-redundant predictor of duration. Sample rows have no procedures and are correctly '0'; no positive samples to verify, but silent-row zeros are reasonable.

per_column.name: has_multiple_meds
per_column.rationale: Medication burden is a reasonable complexity signal, though highly imbalanced (7 positives) limiting leverage. The acne row lists two medications (adapalene + doxycycline) yet is coded '0', suggesting the extraction is unreliable.

per_column.name: note_length
per_column.rationale: Raw character/token length is explicitly named as a generic low-leverage feature; it is trivially derivable and adds little genuine analytical axis beyond the richer complexity columns. Values are directly computable from the text, so groundedness is high.

per_column.name: is_urgent_note
per_column.rationale: A note-derived urgency flag is largely redundant with the existing 'urgency' column, reducing leverage. Groundedness is questionable: two rows explicitly marked Urgent in source are coded '0', showing the derived flag disagrees with stated urgency without clear textual basis.

per_column.name: has_diagnostics
per_column.rationale: Presence of ordered labs/imaging is a strong, non-redundant signal for longer visits. Sample values track the text well: labs/MRI/echo notes are '1', the URI and acne notes without diagnostics are '0'.

judge.rationale: Several columns (num_conditions, has_procedure, has_diagnostics) provide genuine complexity axes well-suited to predicting visit duration, while note_length is generic and is_urgent_note largely restates the existing urgency column. Groundedness is mixed: has_diagnostics and note_length read the text soundly, but num_conditions shows inconsistent counts, has_multiple_meds miscodes a multi-med row as 0, and is_urgent_note contradicts explicitly Urgent source rows, indicating some values assert readings the text does not support.
